assignment_03_key

Author

Bill Perry

Introduction

This analysis examines whether crayfish chelae (claw) length differs between upstream and downstream locations relative to waterfalls across six different rivers. We hypothesize that downstream crayfish will have larger chelae due to increased food availability and different selective pressures.

Study Design: - Fixed effect: Position (Upstream vs Downstream)
- Random effect: River (6 rivers with extreme variation) - Response variable: Chelae length (mm) - Multiple individuals sampled at each position within each river

This analysis demonstrates why mixed-effects models are superior to averaging data and using simple one-way ANOVA.

Generate Example Data with Extreme River Variation

set.seed(42)  # For reproducible results

# Define study parameters
rivers <- paste0("River_", LETTERS[1:6])
positions <- c("Upstream", "Downstream")
n_per_group <- 15  # individuals per position per river

# Generate realistic data with EXTREME river variation and downstream effect
generate_crayfish_data <- function() {
  
  # Create base data structure
  data <- expand_grid(
    river = rivers,
    position = positions,
    individual = 1:n_per_group
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      # Create unique individual IDs
      crayfish_id = paste(river, position, individual, sep = "_"),
      
      # EXTREME river-specific random effects (major differences between rivers)
      river_effect = case_when(
        river == "River_A" ~ rnorm(n(), 3.5, 0.8),   # Very large crayfish
        river == "River_B" ~ rnorm(n(), -4.2, 0.8),  # Very small crayfish
        river == "River_C" ~ rnorm(n(), 5.8, 0.8),   # Extremely large crayfish
        river == "River_D" ~ rnorm(n(), -3.8, 0.8),  # Very small crayfish
        river == "River_E" ~ rnorm(n(), 2.1, 0.8),   # Large crayfish
        river == "River_F" ~ rnorm(n(), -1.5, 0.8)   # Small crayfish
      ),
      
      # Position effect (downstream larger) - consistent across rivers
      position_effect = ifelse(position == "Downstream", 2.8, 0),
      
      # Individual variation
      individual_variation = rnorm(n(), 0, 1.0),
      
      # Calculate chelae length
      chelae_length = 12 + position_effect + river_effect + individual_variation,
      
      # Ensure no negative values
      chelae_length = pmax(chelae_length, 3)
    ) %>%
    select(crayfish_id, river, position, chelae_length)
  
  return(data)
}

# Generate the dataset
crayfish_data <- generate_crayfish_data()

Method 2: CORRECT - Mixed-Effects Model

cat("=== CORRECT METHOD: Mixed-effects model ===\n\n")
=== CORRECT METHOD: Mixed-effects model ===
# Fit the mixed-effects model
model <- lmer(chelae_length ~ position + (1|river), data = crayfish_data)

Direct Comparison of Methods

cat("=== DIRECT COMPARISON OF METHODS ===\n\n")
=== DIRECT COMPARISON OF METHODS ===
# Create comparison table
comparison <- data.frame(
  Method = c("One-way ANOVA (averaged)", "Mixed-effects model"),
  F_statistic = c(round(f_stat_avg, 3), round(f_stat_mixed, 3)),
  DF = c("1, 10", paste0(df_num, ", ", df_den)),
  P_value = c(round(p_value_avg, 3), round(p_value_mixed, 3)),
  Significant = c(ifelse(p_value_avg < 0.05, "Yes", "No"),
                  ifelse(p_value_mixed < 0.05, "Yes", "No")),
  N_observations = c(nrow(averaged_data), nrow(crayfish_data))
)

# Create residual plots using ggplot
residual_data <- data.frame(
  fitted = fitted(model),
  residuals = residuals(model),
  river = crayfish_data$river,
  position = crayfish_data$position
)

# QQ plot for random effects using ggplot
ranef_data <- ranef(model)$river
ranef_df <- data.frame(
  river = rownames(ranef_data),
  intercept = ranef_data[,1]
)

p_qq_ranef <- ggplot(ranef_df, aes(sample = intercept)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(title = "QQ Plot: Random Effects (River Intercepts)",
       x = "Theoretical Quantiles",
       y = "Sample Quantiles") +
  theme_minimal()

# Residuals vs Fitted
p_resid1 <- ggplot(residual_data, aes(x = fitted, y = residuals)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Residuals vs Fitted Values",
       x = "Fitted Values", y = "Residuals")

# Residuals by group

  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Upstream" = "#3498db", "Downstream" = "#e74c3c")) +
  labs(title = "Residuals by Position",

# Residuals by river

# Effect size calculation (Cohen's d for mixed models)
means_by_pos <- crayfish_data %>%
  group_by(position) %>%
  summarise(mean_chelae = mean(chelae_length), .groups = "drop")

# Calculate Cohen's d using the residual SD from the model
residual_sd <- sigma(model)
cohens_d <- diff(means_by_pos$mean_chelae) / residual_sd

cat("Cohen's d effect size:", round(cohens_d, 3), "\n")
Cohen's d effect size: 2.166 
cat("Interpretation:", 
    ifelse(abs(cohens_d) < 0.2, "negligible",
           ifelse(abs(cohens_d) < 0.5, "small",
                  ifelse(abs(cohens_d) < 0.8, "medium", "large"))), "effect\n")
Interpretation: large effect

Visualization Comparing Both Approaches

# Create plots showing why mixed model is better

# Plot 1: Raw data with river structure
p_raw <- ggplot(crayfish_data, aes(x = position, y = chelae_length)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = river), alpha = 0.7, size = 2,
             position = position_jitter(width = 0.2)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = river, color = river), 
            stat = "summary", fun = "mean", size = 1.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "point", size = 4, shape = 21, 
               fill = "white", stroke = 2) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "errorbar", 
               width = 0.1, size = 1.2) +
  labs(title = "Mixed Model Approach: Accounts for River Structure",
       subtitle = "Lines connect river means, black points show overall means ± SE",
       x = "Position", y = "Chelae Length (mm)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead.
# Plot 2: Averaged data approach
p_averaged <- ggplot(averaged_data, aes(x = position, y = mean_chelae)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = river), size = 4, alpha = 0.8,
             position = position_jitter(width = 0.1)) +
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", geom = "point", size = 5, shape = 21, 
               fill = "white", stroke = 2) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "errorbar", 
               width = 0.1, size = 1.2) +
  labs(title = "Naive ANOVA Approach: Treats Rivers as Replicates",
       subtitle = "Only 12 data points, ignores within-river correlation",
       x = "Position", y = "Mean Chelae Length (mm)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

# Combine plots
p_raw / p_averaged

Publication-Quality Figure

# Create summary data for error bars using mixed model predictions
plot_data <- crayfish_data %>%
  group_by(river, position) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_chelae = mean(chelae_length),
    se_chelae = sd(chelae_length) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Create the main figure
final_plot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = position, y = mean_chelae, fill = position)) +
  # Add individual points (raw data) with transparency
  geom_jitter(data = crayfish_data, 
              aes(x = position, y = chelae_length),
              width = 0.25, alpha = 0.3, size = 1.2,
              inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  
  # Add means with error bars
  geom_col(alpha = 0.7, width = 0.6, color = "black", size = 0.5) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean_chelae - se_chelae, 
                    ymax = mean_chelae + se_chelae),
                width = 0.2, size = 0.8) +
  
  # Facet by river
  facet_wrap(~river, ncol = 3, 
             labeller = labeller(river = function(x) gsub("_", " ", x))) +
  
  # Customize colors and theme
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Upstream" = "#2c3e50", "Downstream" = "#c0392b"),
                    name = "Position") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  
  # Labels and theme
  labs(
    title = "Crayfish Chelae Length: Extreme River Variation Requires Mixed Models",
    subtitle = "Mean ± SE shown with individual observations; note massive between-river differences",
    x = "Position Relative to Waterfall",
    y = "Chelae Length (mm)",
    caption = paste0("Mixed-effects model: F(", df_num, ",", round(df_den,1), ") = ", 
                    round(f_stat_mixed, 2), ", p = ", 
                    ifelse(p_value_mixed < 0.001, "< 0.001", round(p_value_mixed, 3)))
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray40"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = "black"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "gray50")
  )

print(final_plot)
# Save the plot
ggsave("crayfish_chelae_mixed_model.png", final_plot, 
       width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
